# pysacd-extract: a drop-in replacement for sacd_extract

`pysacd-extract` takes `sacd_extract`'s options and writes the same files,
with the same names and the same bytes.

## Migrating

<!-- docs-run: group=discs -->
<!-- docs-lint: ignore placeholder -- where pip put pysacd-extract depends on how it was installed (a virtual environment, pipx or pip --user) -->
```sh
mkdir -p ~/bin
ln -s "$(command -v pysacd-extract)" ~/bin/sacd_extract    # that's the whole migration
```

`~/bin` must be on your `PATH`: Fedora and Ubuntu add it in new login shells once the folder
exists.

Scripts, `sacd_extract.cfg` (including `logging=1`) and muscle memory keep
working:

<!-- docs-run: group=discs -->
```console
$ pysacd-extract -2 -m -s -i album.iso       # DSF, stereo + multichannel
$ pysacd-extract -e -C -i album.iso          # DSDIFF edit master + cue + xml
$ pysacd-extract -P -i album.iso             # disc information, as sacd_extract prints it
```

From a PS3, copy the disc and extract it in one pass over the network:

<!-- docs-run: skip="needs a PS3 or a player running SACD Ripper; tools/docs_commands.py runs it against its own pysacd ps3sim" -->
```console
$ pysacd-extract -I -s -i 192.0.2.10:2002
```

Front ends that run `sacd_extract`, such as
[sacd-extract-gui](https://github.com/amstelchen/sacd-extract-gui) and
SACDExtractGUI (its original repository is gone), work unchanged:
point their executable setting at `pysacd-extract`. Programs written in Python
don't need a separate process at all; see [the Python API](api.md).

## Compatibility policy

Differences from `sacd_extract` are treated as bugs. The exceptions below are
deliberate:

| Where | sacd_extract | pysacd-extract | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Two discs aimed at one folder (sets mastered as 1/1, e.g. *Live-Evil*) | mixes them silently, and overwrites tracks whose names match | writes the second disc to `<album> [<catalogue no.>]` and warns; `--disc N/M` gives sacd_extract's own `Disc N` layout | silent mixing is a bug (#4). The discs are told apart by the names and the tags of the files in the folder (album, title, track number and count, ISRC), because `sacd_extract`'s files carry no catalogue number. A tag is compared when the file and the disc both have it. An ISRC on one side only also tells them apart wherever the file would carry the track's ISRC: `sacd_extract`'s ID3 modes 1, 3 and 4 (`id3tag=` in `sacd_extract.cfg`; 4 is the default) write one for every track, blank when the track has none (empty, or the spaces the disc stores), and pysacd's own tags (FLAC, WAV, `--musicbrainz`) write it whenever the track has one. So two editions with the same titles, one with ISRCs and one without, are kept apart (#171). Not compared: a tag that neither side has; the ISRC of files in the minimal ID3 modes (2 and 5), which carry none; an ISRC only a `--musicbrainz` file has, as MusicBrainz supplies ISRCs a disc lacks; and the album, title, track number and count when one side lacks them (`sacd_extract` writes the album title as the title of a track without one). This disc's own files from earlier runs into the folder, in any mode (DSF or DSDIFF tracks, any `-t` selection, `-k` concatenations, the `-e` edit master and its numbered copies), are recognised by the same names and tags, so a later run in another mode writes next to them, as `sacd_extract` does (#165). A file with no tags (`id3tag=0`) or whose tags can't be read is matched by its name alone, which holds the track number and title; for a file that can't be read, a warning says so. **A disc for which all the tags compared are equal is taken for the same disc, and its files are replaced, as `sacd_extract` does.** Use a separate `-o` for two masterings of one album; when the files replaced differ in size from the new ones, a warning says so |
| Hostile disc text (invisible characters such as controls, bidi and zero-width characters, tag characters or U+2028; `` ` $ ; ``; a leading `-`) | copied into names, tags, cue, XML and `-P` as is | neutralised: invisible characters removed (a control becomes a space) and shown as escapes in `-P`; ordinary discs are unaffected | [security](security.md#hostile-text) |
| A title with nothing usable in it (only dots, spaces or control characters), or one whose trimmed form starts with a dot | uses what its trimming leaves: `..`, `.`, a hidden `.name` or an empty name, so the output can land in the parent of the output folder, in the output folder itself or at the filesystem root | never makes `.`, `..` or a name starting with `.`: a leading `.` becomes `_`, an empty album folder is `Unknown Album`, an empty file name is `_`; and it refuses any path outside the output folder. On Windows, which drops trailing dots and spaces from a name, such a name loses them too | output must stay inside the output folder ([security](security.md#hostile-text)); ordinary titles are unaffected |
| A folder or file name that is a Windows device name (`CON`, `PRN`, `AUX`, `NUL`, `COM1`–`COM9`, `LPT1`–`LPT9`, `COM¹`…`LPT³`, also with an extension such as `NUL.x`): in practice a disc titled `CON`, since track names start with their number | the run fails on Windows | on Windows only, gets a leading `_` (`_CON/_CON.cue`), as `pysacd convert` names it; elsewhere such names are ordinary and stay `sacd_extract`'s | Windows can't create these files (#156) |
| Two tracks of one folder whose names would be the same file: tracks past 99, which get no number, with the same title, or with titles that differ only in case (`Intro`, `intro`) on a case-insensitive filesystem (Windows, macOS by default, most SMB shares) | writes the later track over the earlier one | writes the later one as `<name> (2)` (then `(3)`…) and logs it. Whether two names that differ in case are one file is asked of the output folder's filesystem, so on a case-sensitive one (Linux) they stay `sacd_extract`'s; only names equal there too are renamed | no track is lost (#156). Ordinary discs, whose names all differ, are unaffected |
| A relative output folder starting with `./` or `../` (`-o ../out`) | trims the leading dots, which makes it `/out` | uses the folder as given | the folder is the user's choice |
| Malformed TOC timing (a track running past its area's playtime, a zero-length track, more audio than the area's sectors can hold) | uses the times as given: writes a header-only file for a zero-length track and only the frames it finds | cuts tracks to the playtime (so `-P` and the files show the cut times), stops with an error on a zero-length track, on more audio than the image's sectors can hold, or on tracks that together claim that more than twice per format | no real disc does this; a hostile one could ask for hours of output ([security](security.md#hostile-images)) |
| An ISRC field holding a byte outside ASCII (no valid ISRC does) | writes the byte unconverted into UTF-8 tags and XML, which leaves them invalid UTF-8, and drops it from the cue sheet and `-P` | reads it as Latin-1 and writes that character, as before | tags and XML stay valid UTF-8 |
| Korean (KSC 5601) and Chinese GB 2312 disc text | written into names, tags and cue sheets as the raw disc bytes, which aren't UTF-8 | decoded, and written as UTF-8 | names that aren't UTF-8 break most tools and can't be written on macOS or Windows. Shift-JIS and Big5 discs, which `sacd_extract` decodes, are byte-identical (`tests/test_names.py`, #47) |
| Raw-sector images (2064/2054 bytes per sector) | refused | read; `-I` writes a plain ISO | real rips exist in that form |
| A dropped PS3 connection | gives up | reconnects and resumes, after checking it's still the same disc | PS3 drives are flaky |
| Running as root | runs | runs, with a one-line warning | `sacd_extract` users run it with `sudo`; [security](security.md#running-as-root) |
| An area whose only missing frame is its last, after DSD silence (#93) | | fills the frame with silence, warns, and exits 0; any other missing frame still makes the exit status 1. **This is a workaround** for what was seen on early Sony discs (Master TOC 1.00, pressed 2000–2001; four discs of four titles), whose last area sector holds no audio sector header. It may be revisited if other discs show the pattern. The frame before it must be DSD silence: in every 384-bit window of every channel, the count of ones is within 2 of half. On the four discs, those frames deviate by at most 1, while sampled music frames have a median of 24 to 27; with DST kept as stored (`-p`, `-e` without `-c`) that can't be tested, and the run fails as before | the audio is complete: the one filled frame (1/75 s) is silence either way |
| An image cut short inside the audio | stops at the cut, writing what it has | reads up to the cut and writes the rest of each track as silence (counted as missing frames, exit status 1), as long as the run's outputs hold more audio than silence, plus 10 seconds; a run that would be mostly silence (say, only tracks past the cut) stops with an error and writes nothing, unless `--allow-silence` is given | scarletbook's reading of the specification: positions it can't find are missing frames. The limit keeps a sparse or hole-filled image from turning into gigabytes of silence ([security](security.md#hostile-images)) |
| A DST frame the specification calls invalid (for example a code value out of range, sacd-spec corpus `dst-code-all-ones`) | decodes it anyway, into undefined audio | fills it with 0x55, as for any undecodable frame, warns, and counts it as a DST error (exit status 1) | the frame has no defined audio; since 0.3.0 scarletbook decodes, and it applies the specification's validity rules |
| Unreadable frames in a DSDIFF file that keeps DST (`-p`, `-e` without `-c`) | leaves them out | leaves them out too, and also the markers that would fall past the frames the file holds (a track file's index marker at its end, an edited master's later markers) | since 0.4.0 scarletbook lays out the file for the frames it holds, and a marker can't point past them; only on a damaged image |
| `-b` (pauses) | takes each track's boundaries from the sectors where the TOC says the tracks start. Where a track's start sector isn't the one in which its first frame by timecode begins, whole frames move into the neighbouring track, and at some offsets one frame is in neither file (measured on generated discs, a start sector moved by 1 to 9 sectors); a pause whose sectors the TOC gives to the next track opens that track. Where the sectors and the timecodes agree, the files are identical. Frames repeated in both tracks, reported once on a real disc, were not reproduced (#182) | cuts on frame timecodes: the tracks joined are exactly the area's audio | gapless and unambiguous. `tools/extract_compare.py` fails on any such difference: it can only be judged by hand |
| `-z` (no padding): the last file of a chain that stops before the area's last track (the last selected track, a track before one that isn't selected, a `-k` concatenation), when its audio, with the bytes carried into it, ends exactly on a DSF block (4,096 bytes per channel); also a `-z -k` concatenation that holds the area's last track and ends on a block | ends the file one block early and drops that block: its audio is in no file. The DSF header counts the shorter audio | keeps the block in the file | **By decision (#182):** losing audio outranks byte-identity. Every other byte is the same, and `tools/extract_compare.py` counts the file as documented. Elsewhere, where a next file takes the block, the files are byte-identical |
| `-z -k` on a concatenation that holds the area's last track | writes it unpadded: the bytes after its last whole block are dropped (where it ends exactly on a block, see the row above) | pads it, as without `-z` | **Known incompatibility.** scarletbook pads the last file of a chain at the area's end and never shortens it (scarletbook-rs#359). A concatenation that ends before the area's last track is byte-identical, unless it ends exactly on a block (the row above) |
| DSDIFF "creating machine" comment; `.cue`/`.xml` version lines | name sacd-ripper | name pysacd | honesty; otherwise byte-identical |
| Pad byte after odd-length text and ID3 tags in a DSDIFF file | leaves it uninitialised when DST is kept (or with `-e`), so it holds whatever was in memory | writes zero | the byte has no meaning, and it can't be matched |
| Track flags on the `TrackStop` markers of a DSDIFF edited master (`-e`), seen on a real disc whose 5.1 area has gaps between tracks and track mute flags in its TOC (#179) | writes the TOC's mute flags for the track (the flag byte of its length entry) on each `TrackStop`; on that disc 8, "third channel muted" | writes 0 | DSDIFF 1.5 (3.7.2): `TrackFlags` is only meaningful on a `TrackStart`, and must be zero on any other marker. Markers, times and audio are otherwise identical. An area without mute flags, as on most discs, gives the same file |
| Console messages | | `-P` and the cfg summary are identical; other lines are worded differently | |

## Extensions

Extensions are long options only, so they never collide with `sacd_extract`'s
short ones:

- `--flac`, `--wav`: PCM output, gapless, 24-bit;
- `--musicbrainz`: tags and cover art;
- `--submit-isrcs` (with `--musicbrainz`): offer the disc's ISRCs to the
  matched release, asking first ([details](converting.md#submitting-isrcs-to-musicbrainz));
- `--templates`: your own folder and file naming. A file that already exists is kept and counted
  in a closing "skipped" line; `--overwrite` replaces it. If every file was skipped, the exit
  status is 1. A folder that already holds another disc's tracks gets a warning; the folder is
  your template's, so nothing is moved. (With `sacd_extract`'s own naming, a re-run replaces the
  files, as `sacd_extract` does, with a warning when their sizes differ.)
- `--allow-silence`: write the tracks even when most of their audio is missing from the image or
  doesn't decode, as `sacd_extract` does. By default such a run stops
  ([why](security.md#hostile-images)); use it to rescue what a damaged rip still holds;
- `--threads`;
- `--exact`: for a track far into an area, read the area up to it instead of starting
  provisionally ([why](development.md#the-audio-through-scarletbook));
- `--disc N/M`: place a disc mastered as 1/1 into a set;
- `--log-file`, `--log-level`: see [logging](logging.md).

Run `pysacd-extract --help` for the full list.

## Don't take our word for it

<!-- docs-run: skip="needs sacd_extract; tools/docs_commands.py runs it with --sacd-extract" -->
```sh
mkdir a b
(cd a && sacd_extract   -2 -m -s -i ../album.iso)
(cd b && pysacd-extract -2 -m -s -i ../album.iso)
diff -r a b && echo identical
```

**What's checked, and where.** Every pull request runs this comparison on generated discs
(`tests/test_extract_tree.py`): plain DSD, DST and both together, at 2, 5 and 6 channels, in every
`sacd_extract`-compatible mode of `tools/extract_compare.py`, against a `sacd_extract` built from a
pinned commit. Real discs carry far more than a generated one can, so the same tool runs on them by
hand before each release ([releasing](development.md#packaging-and-releases)); CI has no real discs.
The comparison didn't run in CI at all for 0.3.0 to 0.4.3: see the [changelog](../CHANGELOG.md).

On a library of real discs:

- **`-P` disc information:** identical on **99 of 99** plain-SACD images.
- **Output trees:** **28 of 28** end-to-end cases byte-identical. They cover
  every cfg mode, `-o`/`-y`, `-z`, `-k`, `-b`, `-I -w`, 5-channel areas,
  multi-disc sets, titles with trailing spaces, a disc with no text, DSDIFF
  edit masters, cue and XML.
- **DST:** **6,676,925 frames** (27 areas, about 24.7 hours) decoded with no
  errors.
- **Full DST syntax:** every optional feature, forced by a test-only encoder
  at 2, 5 and 6 channels, gives identical results from the original, pysacd
  and `sacd_extract`.
- **PCM:** matches FFmpeg's DSD decoder to −104 dB below 20 kHz. Tracks join
  sample-exactly.

Speed comparisons are in [performance](performance.md).
